situation:
You are to assume the role of general manager of GATE NINE GRILL, a quick-serve restaurant at the north entrance of the Riverside Arena campus. The board chair (judge) of the worker co-operative that owns the restaurant has asked you to recommend how the store should run the ninety minutes before a game.

Gate Nine Grill is owned by the ninety people who cook, serve, and clean in it; the member-owners vote on how shifts and hours are shared. The store sells a short menu of sandwiches, fries, and frozen drinks through a dining room that seats sixty and a drive-thru window facing the arena parking lots.

On event nights the two channels collide. In the ninety minutes before a game the dining room fills with walk-up ticket holders arriving on foot while vehicles stack at the drive-thru, and the single kitchen line cannot keep both moving. Drive-thru times have passed six minutes and cars back onto the campus access road. The store's occupancy permit allows it to close the dining room to walk-in orders once the lobby reaches its posted limit.

The board chair (judge) wants a recommendation. Closing the dining room for that window would clear the drive-thru, but it would turn away the walk-up ticket holders who arrive on foot without a car and would cut the shifts of the member-owners who staff the lobby. Keeping both channels open protects those shifts and those guests, but it leaves drive-thru times where they are and puts the store outside the franchisor's service-time standard, which the franchise agreement requires it to meet.

You will present your recommendation to the board chair (judge) in the board chair's (judge) office. The board chair (judge) will begin by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the board chair's (judge) questions, the board chair (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of board chair (judge) of the worker co-operative that owns GATE NINE GRILL. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the general manager (participant) to recommend how the store should run the ninety minutes before a game, when the dining room and the drive-thru compete for one kitchen line. You want to hear which channel the store should protect, what that choice does to the member-owners who staff the lobby and to the walk-up ticket holders who arrive on foot, and how the recommendation stands against the franchisor's service-time standard.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up carrying the cost of what you are recommending?
Can we defend that to the members who lose hours?
